changes.evidence: The leftmost mark is one short horizontal dash. It is followed by two very compressed letter strokes read ou; there is no tall curved opening parenthesis. The C mark is separately resolved in M1260.
One connected word follows ou: an initial s return, low eu, tall looped l, then e-m-en and an angular terminal t. There are no separate words si on préfère.

The second word has a looped d and tall stem, low ou and an upright terminal t before e: doute. A separate compressed group precedes it. The latter does not expose every letter clearly, so the inherited sans doubt remains.
After l-apostrophe, the low e-n-s run has the same shape as the later l’ens on this leaf, including its terminal downward return. The extra initial e and terminal s are not an un sequence.
Inside the large opening parenthesis, the small s is followed by a short upright i and its upper mark. No a loop or final r follows it before the separate capital S.
After disons there is exactly one large closing curve and one detached full stop. The gap does not contain a second closing parenthesis.

The d has a low loop and tall stem, then a connected rounded return before the separate initial e of extension. That connected return favors a written e rather than a detached apostrophe, so de extension is preferred, with d’extension still possible. The singular ending n has no additional s before the comma.
The initial low n, small a and dotted i are followed by the twin s turns and a low final ance run. This longer word is naissance, followed by a distinct à; it is not lieu.

Both words are live; neither has a cancellation stroke. The separate companion crop is crops/149_scan092_on.png, box [1420,775,1605,890].

One long cancellation crosses the lower word after peut. An initial i mark, an upright t and a substantial middle p descender support interpréter, but several intervening letters are covered. The C doubt is retained; a separate lower précisément is not readable in this span.

The raised word has initial p-r, an accented e, open c, i mark, then s-er. It ends before the space leading to ainsi; there is no following ment. Its descending attachment reaches the cancelled word after peut.
The live word after the cancellation has an a loop, a separate high i stroke, low n, s return and final i mark. The first i rules out aussi; no strike crosses this word.

The initial overworking includes a low loop and tall stroke before the e/n-like run. It may be retracing of the initial e or an extra d, so retain entre first with dentre possible. No separately readable cancelled word is asserted. The crossed t and final r/e are clear.

A short en precedes the word. The ending contains a small a, low n and tall angular final t; there is no terminal ion followed by a separate de. The long stroke below belongs continuously to the g descender.
After the q-u run, a raised apostrophe precedes the o-n strokes. An isolated a and a separate v-u group follow. The tall entry and low return of vu are visible; the phrase is not qui se passe.
After cas is a short accented où, then a separate small s and a distinct est ending in the angular t return. The next word de is separate.
The word has the early t upright, a low r-o run, then a tall d entry followed by u-i-t. There is no p descender of interprète. The last t is an angular rising return.
The final s return is followed by a clean gap before des. No detached point is present, matching the earlier occurrence of l’ens on this leaf.

The subscript has a long left stroke with angular upper and lower right branches, the local K form, rather than an eta hump and descender. A short independent horizontal bar is visibly above it. The bar absent from H is retained.
After s-prime there is a looped d with one low e return, followed by a gap before S-prime with low s. No a-n-s letters are written in that gap.

The first connector is a straight horizontal shaft ending in a small pen lift without angled head strokes. The following three connectors have distinct pointed or turned arrowheads in the same whole-formula crop.
A thin 9 with long curved tail and a separate 1 are written in the lower-left margin, in a finer hand. H’s following explanatory note is editorial and is absent from the manuscript.

second_boxes.reading: naissance à une famille de sections

notes:
The page describes how a section associated with f_K gives a family of sections over the residue fields k(s), then says this correspondence can be made more precise by extending the codimension-one discussion. It introduces the normalisation S' of S in the barred K and identifies the fibre with maximal ideals of the written clôture normale of the local ring. It replaces normalisateur by stabilisateur, writes N_{s'} for that stabiliser, and gives the extension (29) with I_{s'} at its left. This is a summary of the manuscript’s claims, not a mathematical verification. The explicitly written normale and the bar on K in the ambient E group are retained. No proof of the fibre identification or exactness of (29) was attempted; check_events is empty. H’s note about another use of S' on the preceding page is editorial; no other leaf was inspected or used. No author page number is visible on this leaf. There are19 principal source baselines,18 of prose and one display, with two raised replacement words and the separate thin folio91. The opening is a dash rather than a parenthesis, and only one closing parenthesis precedes the first full stop. The compressed sans and the two crossed-out prose words retain doubts. The live entre|dentre is heavily retraced, without a securely separable extra cancelled word. The target in (29) has a clear live replacement E and readable shared k(s). Completed adjudication tentatively reads the earlier crossed group name as Gal; its letters remain low confidence, and the deletion and replacement are now represented as separate layers. The Q has an extra inner stroke within its round body and is encoded as mathbb Q; bold/blackboard and E/mathcal-E wrapper conventions alone are not counted as substantive reading differences. The long low stroke at généralisant is continuous with its g descender. All22 saved detail crops have been viewed once; no decided place was recropped. The anonymous second-reading box for stabilisateur extends above the saved crop to include the full ascender tips, and all mathematical boxes give the full expressions. Root independently reviewed the whole leaf and all22 saved crops and confirmed the final readings. The visibly barred K in the ambient E group may be in mathematical tension with the following stabilizer/inertia extension; that possible tension has not been investigated as a proof check, and the written bar is retained.
Root review: the whole page and all22 saved crops were independently inspected. The singular extension and literal E_barK were confirmed. Final blind adjudication preserves de extension|d’extension and records tentative cancelled Gal beneath the live replacement E in the target of (29).

Blind adjudication gives the target correction in (29) two explicit layers: tentative cancelled Gal beneath the live replacement E, with shared k(s). The underlying letters remain low confidence, but their broader curved remnant, small oval and upright make a candidate possible; this supersedes the first-stage decision to leave the whole target undifferentiated. The singular extension remains; a connected e-like return after d now favors the literal de extension, with d’extension retained as an alternative. The heavily retraced initial of entre also admits dentre. The raised correction remains préciser, since the accented e, open c and i are visible without the l/g of prolonger. Both occurrences of l’ens remain the written short form; no abbreviation point is supplied. The barred K and headless first connector of (29) are retained. All twelve differing boxes were inspected.
